source.title: Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models

accepted.question_text: For the ant-inspired reinforcement models on a finite graph with two marked vertices N (nest) and F (food), where independent random walks start at N, stop when they hit F, and then reinforce either a uniformly selected shortest N-to-F path in the visited subgraph or the loop-erasure of the reversed path, is it true on every finite graph that the only edges whose weights grow linearly in the number of walks are exactly the edges lying on geodesics between N and F?
accepted.context_brief: Geodesic-finding reinforcement on finite graphs

evidence.quote: Our main conjecture is that on any finite graph, with two marked nodes as above, the only edges whose weight will grow linearly are those lying on a geodesic between N and F.
Open Problem 1 Prove the main conjecture above on general finite graphs.

accepted.question_text: Extend the same ant-inspired reinforcement model from finite graphs to the two-dimensional integer lattice Z^2 with a nest N and food vertex F: do the reinforced random walks asymptotically identify geodesic edges, in the sense that only edges on shortest N-to-F paths have weights growing linearly?
accepted.context_brief: Geodesic reinforcement on Z^2

evidence.quote: Open Problem 2 Prove the main conjecture on Z 2 .
the only edges whose weight will grow linearly are those lying on a geodesic between N and F.

accepted.question_text: How can the ant-inspired reinforcement model, in which random walks start from a nest and reinforce paths after reaching food, be extended so that several food sources are handled meaningfully, and what are the features of the limiting reinforced graph when this multi-food-source model is run on Z^2?
accepted.context_brief: Multiple food sources in reinforced walks

evidence.quote: Open Problem 3 Extend the model so that it can take into consideration several sources of food in a meaningful manner. Identify the features of the limiting graph obtained on Z 2 .

accepted.question_text: How can the ant-inspired reinforcement model be extended to transient graphs such as Z^d or regular trees, for example by introducing a density of food sources, adding a weak drift toward the origin, or conditioning walks to hit the set of food sources, and what limiting reinforced structure results in those transient settings?
accepted.context_brief: Reinforcement on transient graphs

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4 Extend the model to transient graphs, such as Z d or regular trees. This could be done by putting a density of sources of food or by considering a walks with a (weak) drift towards the origin, or conditioned to hit the set of sources of food.

accepted.question_text: In super-linear preferential attachment trees with fitness, vertices have i.i.d. weights W_i, a new vertex n attaches to an existing vertex i with probability proportional to f(deg_{n-1}(i), W_i), and f grows super-linearly in degree. The source gives a summability condition for emergence of an infinite star. Is there an analogous general condition, along the same lines, that characterizes emergence of a unique infinite path?
accepted.context_brief: Infinite paths in super-linear preferential attachment with fitness

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5 Can one identify a more general condition, along the lines of (1), for the emergence of an infinite path?
We consider a model of randomly growing trees called super-linear preferential attachment with fitness

accepted.question_text: For super-linear preferential attachment trees with fitness in the regime where the limiting infinite tree T_infty contains a unique infinite path and every vertex has finite degree, determine the growth rates, as the tree grows, of the maximum degree and of the label of the vertex attaining that maximum degree.
accepted.context_brief: Maximum degree in the infinite-path regime

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 In the case the infinite tree T∞ contains an infinite path, what are the growth rates of the maximum degree and the label of the vertex that attains the maximum degree?

accepted.question_text: For super-linear preferential attachment trees with fitness, determine the correct normalization of the empirical degree distribution and identify its scaling limit.
accepted.context_brief: Empirical degree distribution scaling

evidence.quote: Open Problem 7 What is the correct scaling of the empirical degree distribution, and what is its scaling limit?

accepted.question_text: In the super-linear preferential attachment with fitness model, replace the tree growth rule by a multigraph rule in which each new vertex n, at every step n >= 2, chooses m >= 2 existing vertices from T_{n-1} to connect with. How does allowing m multiple attachments per arriving vertex change the phase transition between infinite-star behavior and infinite-path behavior?
accepted.context_brief: Multiple attachments in super-linear preferential attachment

evidence.quote: Open Problem 8 If at every step n ≥ 2, vertex n were to choose m ≥ 2 many vertices from Tn−1 to connect with, creating a multigraph rather than a tree, how would this influence the phase transition?

accepted.question_text: Consider the reinforced sequence on positive reals with parameter 0 < beta < 1: X_0 is sampled from a probability distribution mu, and given X_0,...,X_{n-1}, X_n is either sampled independently from mu with probability beta or sampled from the previous values with probability proportional to the value times its local time. When mu has bounded support with essential supremum 1 and mu({1})=0, lambda_* is the almost-sure limit of the empirical mean. Is there a central limit theorem, or other limit theorem, describing the fluctuations of sum_{i=1}^n (X_i - lambda_*)?
accepted.context_brief: Fluctuations for bounded-support reinforced sequences

evidence.quote: Open Problem 9 Is there a (central) limit theorem describing the fluctuations of n ∑ i=1 (Xi −λ ∗ )?
Take a probability distribution µ on the positive reals, let 0 < β < 1, and sample a sequence as follows

accepted.question_text: In the bounded-support reinforced sequence model with essential supremum 1, mu({1})=0, and innovation probability beta, the source gives a criterion beta * integral dmu(x)/(1-x) >= 1 for existence of the mean-limit equation; if that criterion fails, mass escapes to the endpoint 1. In that failure case, can one prove a limit theorem describing the behavior around the point 1, for example under regular variation of x -> mu((1-x,1)) near x=0?
accepted.context_brief: Condensation near endpoint one

evidence.quote: Open Problem 10 In the case that (3) fails, is there a limit theorem around the point one?
This is because mass escapes at one, a condensation effect.

accepted.question_text: In the reinforced sequence model with innovation probability beta and an unbounded-support base distribution mu on the positive reals, compactly supported test functions see only beta times mu in the limiting empirical measure and a proportion 1-beta of mass escapes to infinity. Since the empirical average n^{-1} sum_{i=1}^n X_i diverges, what is the superlinear rate at which sum_{i=1}^n X_i tends to infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Growth speed for unbounded-support reinforced sequences

evidence.quote: Open Problem 11 Determine the speed at which (∑ n i=1 Xi) goes to infinity.
so the speed must be superlinear.

accepted.question_text: For a WARM, a graph-based interacting Polya urn on a graph G=(V,E) with bounded firing rates p(v), edge counts N_e(t), and reinforcement weight W(x)=x^alpha, suppose alpha < 1. On infinite graphs, is there a unique equilibrium x, and does each scaled edge weight X_e(t)=N_e(t)/t converge almost surely to x_e?
accepted.context_brief: Sublinear WARM equilibrium on infinite graphs

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. On infinite graphs there is a unique equilibrium x and Xe(t) → xe for every e ∈ E almost surely.
These problems are devoted to the study of the so-called (W,α)-reinforcement models, or WARMs for short

accepted.question_text: For the critical WARM with alpha = 1 on the integer-line graph G=Z and uniform firing rates p(v)=1, do the scaled reinforced edge weights converge almost surely to the constant equilibrium 1 at every location, i.e. does x_v(t) -> 1 for all v as t -> infinity?
accepted.context_brief: Critical WARM on Z

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2. For G = Z with firing rates p(v) ≡ 1, one has almost surely ∀v xv(t) → 1, as t → ∞.

accepted.question_text: For finite-graph WARMs with strong reinforcement alpha > 1, the source states that when alpha > 2 every connected component of the limiting support should be a tree. Can the lower bound alpha > 2 be improved, and if so what is the sharp threshold above which every connected component of the surviving-edge support is a tree?
accepted.context_brief: Tree support threshold for strong WARM

evidence.quote: Open Problem 12 Improve the lower bound α > 2 for which every connected component is a tree.

accepted.question_text: For finite-graph WARMs with strong reinforcement alpha > 1 and uniform firing rates p(v)=1, the source states that for alpha > 25 each connected component of the limiting support is a whisker, meaning a tree of diameter at most 3. Can the lower bound alpha > 25 be improved, and what is the sharp threshold for this whisker property?
accepted.context_brief: Whisker support threshold for strong WARM

evidence.quote: Open Problem 13 Improve the lower bound α > 25 for which (when p(v) ≡ 1) every connected component is a whisker.
a whisker, a tree graph of diameter at most 3

accepted.question_text: For an infinite-graph WARM with reinforcement exponent alpha > 1 and firing rates p(v) bounded both away from zero and away from infinity, does the limit of every scaled edge weight X_e(t) exist almost surely, do the surviving edges form only finite connected components, and in the case alpha > 2 are those finite surviving components necessarily trees?
accepted.context_brief: Strong WARM percolation with bounded firing rates

evidence.quote: Conjecture 3. Assume that firing rates p(v) are bounded away from zero and from infinity, and that α > 1. Then the limit limt→∞ Xe(t) exists almost surely for each e, and the surviving edges form finite connected components. In particular, for α > 2 they are trees.

accepted.question_text: For a WARM on the integer lattice graph G=Z^d with d >= 2 and reinforcement exponent alpha > 1, can one choose a bounded firing-rate function p that is not bounded away from zero so that the set of surviving edges contains an infinite connected component almost surely or with positive probability? If such an infinite surviving component can occur, is it unique?
accepted.context_brief: Infinite surviving components in lattice WARMs

evidence.quote: Open Problem 14 Do there exist a bounded (but not bounded away from 0) function p, d ≥ 2, and α > 1 for which the WARM on the graph G = Z d almost surely (or indeed with positive probability) contains an infinite connected component of surviving edges? If such a component exists, is it unique?

accepted.question_text: Consider a vertex-reinforced random walk on the integers that jumps to nearest neighbors, starts with weight one at each vertex, and from location x at time n jumps to x+1 with probability proportional to w(1+ell_n(x+1)), where ell_n(y) is the local time at y by time n. If the weight function is sublinear in the sense that w(x)=o(x^alpha) for some alpha < 1, is the walk recurrent?
accepted.context_brief: Sublinear vertex-reinforced random walk on Z

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15 Suppose that w(x) = o(x α ) for some α < 1. Is this process recurrent?
Consider a vertex reinforced random walk on the integers

accepted.question_text: For a network of N >= 2 interacting reinforced stochastic processes with two actions S={0,1}, weighted adjacency matrix A, and dynamics Z_{n+1}=(1-r_r-r_f)Z_n+r_r X_{n+1}+r_f p with conditional mean E[X_{n+1}|F_n]=A^T Z_n, where r_f represents a forcing input toward p and r_r represents reinforcement, determine whether the discrete-time process Z_n fails to converge and whether it can be rescaled to a well-defined continuous-time interacting Wright-Fisher-type limit when r_f is asymptotic to c r_r^2. If such a limit exists, give a mathematically meaningful formulation of its dynamics and asymptotic behavior.
accepted.context_brief: Interacting decaying Polya urns with forcing input

evidence.quote: It is also very interesting to understand whether or not the discrete-time process (Zn)n could be rescaled in order to get a proper time-continuous limiting process (Yt)t.
although the meaning of this dynamics and the asymptotic properties of this time-rescaled process are unknown at the moment.

accepted.question_text: In preferential attachment models that allow vertex and/or edge removal, rather than pure growth where added vertices and edges remain forever, how do specific removal mechanisms affect global network quantities beyond the expected degree sequence, especially the component structure, existence of a giant component, and persistence or time-variation of the vertex of maximal degree?
accepted.context_brief: Preferential attachment with removal

evidence.quote: It would be interesting to analyse the effect of vertex and/or edge removal on other quantities, such as the component structure and the vertex of maximal degree.
For a given choice of removal mechanism, does the network contain a giant component? Is the vertex with maximal degree persistent, or does it change with time?

accepted.question_text: Compare the local weak limits of two preferential-attachment-type models: the Bernoulli preferential attachment model BPA(f), in which a new vertex connects independently to each existing vertex v with probability f(D_v^{in}(n-1))/(n-1), and a preferential attachment model with random out-degrees adapted to use only in-degree and an i.i.d. Poisson number of outgoing edges with matching parameter. Under the corresponding parameter choices, do the local limits of these two models agree, and can the different existing descriptions of their local limits be made equivalent?
accepted.context_brief: Local limits of Bernoulli and random-out-degree preferential attachment

evidence.quote: What is the relation between the local limits of the two models?
It can be expected that these agree, provided we appropriately adapt the preferential attachment model with random out-degrees studied in [17].

accepted.question_text: For preferential attachment models with general attachment functions f beyond the affine case, and with a fixed number m > 1 of out-edges per arriving vertex, identify and prove the local weak limits. In particular, extend beyond the known tree case m=1 despite the absence, for graph models with m>1, of both the continuous-time branching-process embedding used for trees and the Polya urn representations available in the affine case.
accepted.context_brief: Local limits beyond affine preferential attachment

evidence.quote: Open Problem 24 (Local limits preferential attachment models beyond the affine case)
The local limits for such models, but now with a fixed number of out-edges per vertex, has not been considered beyond the tree case for which m = 1

trace.notes: Normalized ARGUMENTS as the single zbMATH resolver URL https://zbmath.org/8157796 with identifier 8157796.

Local shard metadata identified the exact work as 'Open problems in stochastic reinforcement models' with DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-76738-8_29. Exact-title web recovery found the MATRIX-hosted PDF Aletti.pdf, whose visible title and DOI/page listing match the same work. Shell curl to api.zbmath.org failed because DNS/network access is unavailable in the sandbox, so the readable MATRIX PDF URL was used as the primary source artifact.

Mapped the 22-page PDF: title/abstract and introduction on page 1; Section 2 geodesic-finding reinforcement on pages 1-3; Section 3 super-linear preferential attachment with fitness on pages 3-6; Section 4 reinforced sequences on pages 6-8; Section 5 WARMs on pages 8-12; Section 6 sub-linear vertex-reinforced random walk on page 12; Section 7 networks of reinforced stochastic processes on pages 12-17; Section 8 preferential attachment models on pages 17-22. Likely open-question regions are Open Problems 1-16 and 22-24 plus Conjectures 1-3.
Extracted Open Problems 1-4 on geodesic-finding reinforcement algorithms, Z^2, multiple food sources, and transient graphs.

Extracted Open Problems 5-8 on infinite-path criteria, maximum-degree growth, empirical degree distribution scaling, and multi-attachment phase transitions in super-linear preferential attachment with fitness.
Extracted Open Problems 9-11 on central/endpoint limit theorems and superlinear growth speed for reinforced sequences.
Extracted Conjectures 1-3 and Open Problems 12-14 on WARM equilibria, critical behavior on Z, strong-reinforcement support thresholds, and infinite surviving components on Z^d.
Extracted Open Problem 15 on recurrence of sub-linear vertex-reinforced random walk on Z.
Extracted Open Problem 16 as the problem of analyzing interacting exponentially decaying Polya urns with forcing input and possible continuous-time scaling limits.
Extracted Open Problems 22-24 on preferential attachment with removal, relationships between Bernoulli and random-out-degree local limits, and local limits beyond affine attachment functions.
